articles.title: GitHub Copilot app for Beginners: How to teach Copilot about your codebase
articles.summary:
GitHub Copilot app for Beginners: How to teach Copilot about your codebase
Learn how to add custom instructions and skills to your repository, use custom agents, and connect MCP servers like Playwright.
Context matters when you’re working with AI. Every codebase has its own house rules: how components are structured, which scripts to run, and which conventions apply to different frameworks and file types.
Copilot can help you make changes across a project, but it works best when it knows those rules, too. Much of that knowledge can live inside the repository, so Copilot can pick it up automatically instead of requiring you to explain the same standards, scripts, and workflows every time you start a new task.
In this installment of our GitHub Copilot app for Beginners series, we’ll look at four ways to tailor how Copilot works with your project:
- Custom instructions communicate the conventions Copilot should follow.
- Agent skills package repeatable procedures.
- Custom agents bring specialized guidance to larger tasks.
- Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers connect Copilot to external tools and data sources, expanding what it can do.
Let’s look at how each one works and how they can work together.
Start with custom instructions
Suppose you ask Copilot to add a custom page size to an application. Making the change is only part of the job. The new code should also follow the patterns your team already uses.

articles.title: OCP Global Summit: Amid Ecosystem Adoption, NVIDIA Opens Vera Rubin Architecture to Help Scale AI Factories Worldwide

Together, these efforts span the AI factory itself, the utility grid that powers it and the rack-scale architecture at the heart of modern accelerated computing.
NVIDIA and Partners Announce Open Architecture Advances

- NVIDIA and hyperscalers published open standards for next-generation AI factories, including AI factory design standards and grid resilience.

articles.title: Filter, reshape, and redact logs before export with Transformers
articles.summary:
Filter, reshape, and redact logs before export with Transformers
Logpush delivers logs in batches as quickly as possible, enabling Cloudflare to provide information almost in real time. During our recent Birthday Week, we made Logpush available on all self-serve plans and Transformers generally available.
Those changes were among eight major updates to Cloudflare Observability and reflect our commitment to make every Cloudflare feature available to everyone. This post takes a deeper look at how Transformers work inside Logpush's export pipeline. Observability teams use Logpush to export Cloudflare logs to security information and event management systems (SIEMs), analytics platforms, and object storage. Before those logs reach their destination, teams may need to remove health checks, omit sensitive fields, or reshape records for dashboards and investigations. Today, this often requires a separate processing service that teams must deploy, scale, monitor, and maintain.
For example, a team that collects logs from multiple CDNs can add a static provider field to normalize records before they reach its analytics platform. Teams also pay to export, ingest, and store records they discard as soon as they arrive, so filtering them before delivery can reduce downstream data volume and cost.

articles.title: Run multi-node inference workloads using Ray LLM Deep Learning Containers | Amazon Web Services
articles.summary:
Artificial Intelligence
Run multi-node inference workloads using Ray LLM Deep Learning Containers
This post shows how to deploy one large language model (LLM) across two GPU nodes on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) with the multi-node Ray LLM Deep Learning Containers. It uses separate prefill and decode nodes behind one OpenAI-compatible endpoint. This kind of multi-node setup is common for tensor, pipeline, and data parallelism, as well as prefill/decode disaggregation inference workloads. In a previous post, we introduced the Ray Serve DLC and used it to stand up a small model behind an HTTP endpoint on a single GPU node. You had a working inference endpoint, and the container keeps the GPU stack compatible, including CUDA libraries, so you did not need to write boilerplate code.
Ray is a distributed compute framework, so Ray Serve deployments can span multiple nodes. Customers use multi-node Ray Serve for several reasons. Some want to run foundation or open-weight models that are too large for a single GPU. Others need more throughput than one replica can deliver. Still others want to separate the two phases of inference to improve performance. In each case, customers must build the dependency chain themselves: choosing compatible libraries for the GPU stack and debugging issues when a component drifts out of alignment. This is undifferentiated work that takes time and effort away from delivering models.

articles.title: IA cria bots ultra-realistas para enganar golpistas em chamadas
articles.summary:
Uma empresa australiana está usando inteligência artificial para fazer golpistas perderem tempo com vítimas que não existem. A Apate desenvolveu robôs que conversam com criminosos por telefone e pela internet para reunir informações sobre fraude e dificultar novas abordagens.
A tecnologia também está sendo aplicada em armadilhas digitais que atraem hackers. A proposta é aproveitar a capacidade da IA de imitar comportamentos humanos para tornar essas estratégias de defesa mais eficazes.
Robôs que fingem ser vítimas
A Apate desenvolve a plataforma há dois anos. Segundo Dali Kaafar, fundador e CEO da empresa, o sistema reúne cerca de 350 mil robôs e é utilizado por bancos, com apoio de companhias de telecomunicações.
Os programas atendem ligações, respondem a mensagens de texto e participam de grupos on-line usados para aplicar golpes. Durante as conversas, podem reunir informações sobre as atividades criminosas. A empresa afirma ter coletado mais de 250 mil registros em tempo real, incluindo endereços de sites fraudulentos, dados bancários e contas usadas para movimentar dinheiro ilegal.
Para não levantar suspeitas, os robôs assumem diferentes perfis e comportamentos. Alguns usam WhatsApp; outros não. Há os que atendem o telefone e os que encerram a conversa, dizendo que retornarão mais tarde.
Gostamos de pensar que estamos construindo as vítimas perfeitas para os golpistas.

articles.title: Microsoft: Windows 11 23H2 reaches end of support in 30 days
articles.summary:
Microsoft has reminded customers that systems running Windows 11 23H2 Enterprise, Education, and IoT Enterprise editions will stop receiving security updates next month.
The announcement follows the end of support for Windows 11 23H2 Home and Pro editions in November 2025.
Users are now advised to upgrade to Windows 11 26H2 (also known as the Windows 11 2026 Update), which became generally available in September 2026 as an enablement package (eKB) and will reach end of support for consumers in October 2029.
"The November 2026 Windows security update will be the last update available for these editions. After this date, devices running these editions will no longer receive monthly security updates containing protections from the latest security threats," it said in a message center update. "We recommend updating eligible devices running Windows 11, version 23H2 to a supported version of Windows 11."
Windows 11 26H2 is now available in a phased rollout to eligible Windows 11 devices for those who have enabled the "Get the latest updates as soon as they're available" setting.
"If the update is ready for your device, it will download and install automatically, and a single restart will complete the process," Microsoft added.
You can also manually check if the update is available by clicking "Check for updates" in the Settings > Windows Update section. If the system is ready to update, you'll see the option to "Download and install Windows 11, version 26H2."

articles.title: ReplaySSM: Rethinking State Storage for Faster Hybrid-Model Decoding | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.summary:
Hybrid models interleave state-space model (SSM) layers with a few attention layers. NVIDIA Nemotron 3, Qwen3.5 through Qwen3.8, Kimi-K3, and GLM-5.3-Flash are all built this way, with Mamba-2, Gated DeltaNet (GDN), or Kimi Delta Attention (KDA) as the SSM layer.
SSM layers are designed to make decoding fast: they use a fixed-size state in place of a key-value (KV) cache that grows with context length. At serving batch sizes, however, the SSM layers, not attention, can be the latency bottleneck up to 100K tokens of context. SSM layers also complicate two techniques that reliably speed up attention decoding: speculative decoding and quantization.
ReplaySSM makes SSM layers the fast part again. It represents the SSM state as a checkpoint plus a buffer of recent inputs. This separates output computation from state updates and addresses three challenges in current SSM decoding: state traffic, rollback for speculative decoding, and error accumulation in a quantized state.
ReplaySSM is joint work between NVIDIA and the Dao AI Lab at Princeton. The paper, ReplaySSM: Cache SSM Inputs, Not State, details all three benefits and presents the full evaluation. It is available on arXiv, with code on GitHub. It is integrated into NVIDIA TensorRT-LLM, vLLM, and FlashInfer, and also runs in production in GLM-5.3-Flash and Kimi-K3.

articles.title: Fervo’s Utah Geothermal Plant Starts Sending Clean Power To The Grid
articles.summary:
This article was originally published by Canary Media.
The geothermal startup Fervo Energy is now selling power to the grid from its Cape Station project in Utah — marking the first time a utility-scale, next-generation geothermal facility has achieved such a feat worldwide.
The Houston-based firm turned on an initial 33-megawatt unit late last week and has been testing and ramping up output since then. On Thursday, Fervo will officially begin commercial operations, supplying carbon-free electricity to Shell Energy, a retail power provider in California.
Cape Station, a $2 billion project that will eventually be 500 MW, is unique among the world’s commercial geothermal plants. While other facilities draw on naturally occurring hot water and steam, Fervo has engineered its own geothermal resource deep underground. The startup uses drilling techniques from the oil and gas industry to create reservoirs in hot, dry rocks that generate steam to produce electricity.
“Traditional geothermal would have never been done in southern Utah,” says Dawn Owens, Fervo’s senior vice president and head of development and commercial markets.
With the first unit online, Fervo says it is working to commission two more 33-MW power blocks by 1 January, 2027. The project’s remaining 400 MW — which is supported by a new agreement with Google — is under construction and slated to come online in 2028.

articles.title: Andrej Karpathy says only 5,000 people have seen what AI can really do
articles.summary:
Andrej Karpathy says only 5,000 people have seen what AI can really do
OpenAI founding member Andrej Karpathy, who joined Anthropic in May, thinks most of the world has little idea of what AI can do, and in a Sunday post on X, he said the gap is getting wider. By his own napkin math, roughly 6 billion people have barely used an LLM, 1 to 2 billion use chatbots casually, about 20 million use frontier models professionally in math and code, and around 5,000 have access to frontier systems inside the labs.
Box CEO Aaron Levie sees an opportunity in that gap. “This is a good way to understand how early we actually are in AI diffusion right now,” he wrote in his response on X.
He argued that most people still think of AI as a chatbot or a next-generation search engine while barely exploring its more advanced opportunities.
Box bets on agent swarms
“Agent swarms represent possibly the ultimate form factor of what agents will do inside of our workflows,” Levie wrote, envisioning systems that divide complex work among agents running in parallel.
“Agent swarms represent possibly the ultimate form factor of what agents will do inside of our workflows”
For now, “less than a fraction of a fraction of the population uses AI in this way,” Levie noted, and he identified the obstacles keeping it that way. We’re still early. articles.title: Startup Funding: Q3 2026
articles.summary:
80 startups raised $8.5B in Q3, with big hauls by companies tackling data movement and memory.
AI dominated funding in the third quarter of 2026, with two inference companies each announcing $1 billion in funding. But with the data center buildout driving insatiable demand for memory, investors also rewarded startups with alternatives to costly, capacity-limited HBM. Some are building on commodity DRAM or holding models in on-chip SRAM, while others stack memory directly onto compute.
Data movement at all levels of the stack remains a critical bottleneck, too. Interconnect technologies, networking chips, and photonics were the most active areas of the quarter, with startups tackling the problem with diverse approaches ranging from manufacturing-ready co-packaged optics, millimeter-wave RF signals over plastic waveguides, and ferroelectric glass modulators to optical couplers printed directly onto chips and coherent DSPs designed specifically for AI optics.
Nearly $7.5 billion of the quarter’s total was directed to just 22 startups that raised $100 million or more, including eight that saw investors return within roughly a year, some more than doubling the previous round. Plus, agentic EDA and AI-generated analog layout, small chip fabs, diamond-based defect inspection, large-area nanoimprint lithography, and memory-safe microcontrollers feature in this look at 80 companies that collectively raised over $8.5 billion in Q3 2026.

articles.title: Let’s Encrypt Cuts Default Certificate Validity to 64 Days Ahead of 45-Day Switch
articles.summary:
Open Certificate Authority (CA) Let’s Encrypt is taking the first step towards reducing the validity period of the certificates it issues.
Beginning February 10, 2027, it will issue certificates with 64-day lifetimes by default, in preparation for 45-day lifetimes planned for 2028.
In line with the CA/Browser Forum Baseline Requirements, the shorter certificate validity period is expected to improve security on the web by making revocation more efficient and limiting the scope of compromise.
All publicly trusted CAs will make similar changes, Let’s Encrypt noted in a December 2025 blog, when it revealed the planned timeline for switching to 45-day certificates.
Last week, the CA announced that, after February 10, 2027, all newly issued or renewed certificates will have a 64-day validity period, with the last 90-day certificate expected to expire on May 11, 2027.
This week, Let’s Encrypt will start issuing 64-day certificates in its staging environment for testing purposes, and recommends that all customers perform similar tests before the change enters production.
“If your renewals are automated and your client supports ACME Renewal Info (ARI), you should be all set since ARI allows Let’s Encrypt to tell your client when to renew (you can review your ACME client’s documentation to determine if ARI is implemented),” Let’s Encrypt notes.

articles.summary:

Earlier this year, Koho raised $130 million CAD as part of its quest to move from challenger bank to an actual bank.

articles.title: A Spanish museum built a Cray-1 replica powered by 30 old Mac minis
articles.summary:
In a nutshell: A Spanish computing museum has built a working cluster of 30 Mac minis inside a full-size replica of the Cray-1 supercomputer. Most of the Macs are from 2012, but together they have reached a reported 1.3 teraflops in matrix-multiplication tests. Visitors can watch calculations run on a single core before seeing the workload distributed across the cluster.
The Museo de Historia de la Computación spent 18 months developing the exhibit. The replica preserves the appearance of the 1976 machine without trying to reproduce its internal hardware. Built to mark the 50th anniversaries of the Cray-1 and Apple's founding, the model is now on permanent display at the museum alongside two unused authentic Cray CX1 systems.
The cluster contains five quad-core Intel Core i7 machines and 25 dual-core Core i5 models. All but two units, which date to 2014, were made in 2012. That configuration provides 70 cores, although only 64 were active in the most recent tests after one node went offline.
The museum previously reported 1.5 teraflops with all 70 cores running. Both results came from a custom Python matrix-multiplication script, so the figures reflect performance on that test rather than across a range of applications.
A master Mac mini in the exhibit's control terminal coordinates the other machines. The team chose macOS Mojave 10.14 instead of Linux, using the Message Passing Interface (MPI) to handle communication between nodes.

What just happened? The FCC's crackdown on Chinese electronics testing labs continues to move forward, this time with a proposed deadline for cutting them out of the US approval process. The commission will vote on October 29 on rules that would force manufacturers to move testing out of mainland China by December 2028. With 82% of devices authorized last year tested in the Asian nation, it could be a relocation headache for the companies affected.
The restrictions would cover test labs and certification bodies in countries that deny reciprocal treatment to their US counterparts. Chairman Brendan Carr says fewer than 4% of electronic devices are tested in American labs.
If this all sounds familiar, there's a reason. In May 2025, the FCC initially targeted labs owned, controlled, or directed by blacklisted companies and foreign adversary governments. There was also a separate proposal to extend restrictions to every lab in China.
In April 2026, the FCC voted to advance broader restrictions and seek public comment. The latest action would turn that proposal into adopted rules, assuming commissioners approve the draft, with a transition ending December 1, 2028.
Compared with the original 2025 restrictions, the broader proposal focuses on where the testing happens. Under the draft, recognition would be limited to labs in the US or economies with reciprocal recognition agreements. That means a Western company operating a lab in mainland China would still be affected.

articles.title: Critical SonicWall Vulnerability Exploited Days After Disclosure

Threat actors started exploiting a recently patched critical vulnerability in SonicWall SMA1000 appliances within days after public disclosure.
Tracked as CVE-2026-102255 (CVSS score of 10), the security defect is described as a pre-authenticated server-side request forgery (SSRF) issue affecting the SMA1000 Work Place interface.
According to SonicWall, an unintended alternate access path could allow a remote attacker “to direct the appliance to issue requests on their behalf and reach internal functionality and perform unauthorized operations.”
The company disclosed CVE-2026-102255 on October 6, urging customers to update their 6210, 7210, and 8200v models to software versions 12.5.0-03082 and 12.4.3-03670.
On Friday, threat intelligence firms Previdian (formerly KEVIntel) and Defused warned of the first exploitation attempts targeting the security bug.
Defused said that the first exploitation attempts reached its SMA decoys on October 8, only two days after public disclosure.
“SonicWall SMA1000 exploitation attempts are now being observed by Previdian sensors, consistent with CVE-2026-102255 (CVSS 10.0). The vulnerability allows unauthenticated server-side request forgery (SSRF),” Previdian said.
Successful exploitation of the flaw could allow attackers to take over vulnerable devices, cybersecurity firm Horizon3.ai warned.

Marvell Structera X 3406 and 3506 CXL 3.2 Memory Expanders
Patrick gave us the decoder for the models:
- CXL 3 support is indicated by the first digit 3, just as the 2 in last year’s 2404 and 2504 marked CXL 2.0.
- 5 or 4, is the DDR generation
- The trailing two digits are the memory channel count.
Structera X 3406 is therefore a CXL 3 DDR4 part with six channels, while the 3506 is the CXL 3 DDR5 part, also at six channels. This announcement covers only the Structera X memory expansion line, not the Structera A near-memory compute controller that Marvell showed us last year. Still, CXL is focused on optimizing either bandwidth per core (since CXL bandwidth is in addition to native DDR bandwidth) and also capacity expansion.
PCIe Gen6 infrastructure and CXL 3.2 means we get roughly twice the bandwidth over the link, so that is how Marvell is adding more bandwidth from more memory channels.

When we put together the 2026 Future of Platform Engineering report, we weren’t trying to settle the trade-off; we were trying to find out whether platform feature-sourcing decisions revealed anything about the platform team. It turns out it does. Across responses from 379 platform professionals, we found that teams predominantly building from scratch are less likely to have a clear strategy in place and to meet fewer of their platform goals.
This question has changed considerably with AI. Agents have made building easier than ever; an internal tool that once took months to build can now be put together in a day. articles.title: Des lueurs rouges dans le ciel corse : que sont ces « farfadets » capturés en photo ?
articles.summary:
Les images font le tour du web ce matin du lundi 12 octobre 2026. D’étranges formes rouges ont été prises en photo dans le ciel français, au-dessus de la Corse. Elles datent pourtant de la mi-septembre. On les doit à Florian Riou, photographe de montagne et de phénomènes naturels.
Sur son compte Instagram, il explique avoir obtenu ces images du phénomène le 16 septembre dernier, à proximité de Calvi en Corse. Plus précisément, c’est le village de Montemaggiore que l’on aperçoit en dessous de ce spectacle lumineux. Mais alors, que voit-on exactement ?
Des « sprites » ou farfadets dans le ciel : de quoi s’agit-il ?
Ces curieuses formes rougeâtres sont des « sprites », que l’on traduit par farfadets en français. Comme le résume l’Organisation météorologique mondiale (OMM), ce sont des « décharges électriques de grande ampleur » qui « se produisent dans la haute atmosphère ». Ces phénomènes lumineux éphémères apparaissent entre 50 et 90 kilomètres d’altitude environ, « au-dessus de systèmes orageux de grande envergure ».
Mais pourquoi ces lueurs sont-elles rouges ? Selon cet article de l’étudiant en sciences de l’atmosphère Nicholas Buckley, ces lumières rouges apparaissent lorsque l’orage envoie de l’électricité très haut dans le ciel, ce qui fait briller l’azote présent dans l’air quand il est frappé par des électrons.
Le phénomène a longtemps échappé aux scientifiques. Des pilotes en décrivaient depuis des décennies, mais la première preuve visuelle ne date que du 6 juillet 19…

AirPods 5 are Apple’s entry-level earphones what we call an open-ear fit because they don’t have a silicon tip that creates a seal in your ear.
They are designed to just rest comfortably inside your ear.
We know these aren’t everybody’s cup of tea because people are worried they’re going to fall out of the ear.
The people in this camp will pay extra for the AirPods Pro 3, which has the silicon tip that makes them feel a little bit more secure in your ears.
Now this is all well and good but if you’re overlooking the AirPods 5 for that one reason you could be making a huge mistake.
AirPods 5 have the same look and fit as AirPods 4 but their shape and size made them a comfortable fit for us.

articles.title: GitLab warns of max severity code execution vulnerability
articles.summary:
GitLab warned users today to immediately patch a maximum-severity vulnerability in the CI/CD Regular Expression Compiler that could let remote attackers run arbitrary code on targeted instances.
Tracked as CVE-2026-97229, this critical security flaw was discovered by a security researcher using the 'joaxcar' handle and reported via GitLab's HackerOne bug bounty program.
CVE-2026-97229 stems from an integer overflow weakness in GitLab's CI/CD Regular Expression Compiler, which parses, compiles, and evaluates regular expressions in projects' pipeline configuration files.
"GitLab has remediated an issue that, under certain conditions, could have allowed an unauthenticated user to execute arbitrary code on the GitLab server via a specially crafted regular expression in a CI/CD configuration, due to insufficient regular expression validation," the company explained in a Monday advisory.
GitLab fixed the security issue in GitLab Community Edition (CE) and Enterprise Edition (EE) versions from 19.2 before 19.2.8, 19.3 before 19.3.4, and 19.4 before 19.4.2, and urged users to patch their servers immediately.
"These versions contain important bug and security fixes, and we strongly recommend that all self-managed GitLab installations be upgraded to one of these versions immediately," it warned. "GitLab.com is already running the patched version. GitLab Dedicated customers do not need to take action."

The takeaway: A Canadian software engineer who built a camera to identify police cars says two officers came to his home to ask why he was tracking them. They were concerned that repeated observations could expose their routines – the same information that makes searchable vehicle records useful to police and troubling to people being watched.
Anthony Sistilli described Peel Regional Police's visit last month in a YouTube video that he recently posted. His project uses automatic license plate recognition, or ALPR – the technology police use to record passing vehicles and search for them later. But Sistilli designed his camera to pick out police vehicles rather than collect plates from all traffic.
Sistilli built the prototype with a $180 camera and used AI coding tools to develop its software. The first version struggled to process 4K footage while identifying vehicles and reading their license plates. He lowered the resolution and split the work into two stages: first detect a police car, then try to read its plate.
That change reduced the amount of footage the plate-recognition software had to examine. It also made vehicle classification a prerequisite for capturing license plate data. The system would attempt a read only after deciding that a vehicle was a police car.
Sistilli said the officers were polite but worried that someone could use the information to target them. He told them those were the same concerns civilians had about license-plate surveillance. According to…

articles.title: CRA & Chip Design: The New Compliance Standard - EE Times
articles.summary:
Europe’s Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) will soon require chipmakers to prove their silicon is secure. The tools to produce that proof already exist, but they were built for a different purpose.
Europe goes first, again
On Sept. 11, the first operational part of the EU’s Cyber Resilience Act went live. From that day, any company selling a product with digital elements in Europe must flag actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe security incidents within 24 hours, with a fuller report within 72 hours, through a new reporting platform run by the EU’s cybersecurity agency, ENISA. The duty covers products already on the market, including ones shipped years ago. The rest of the law, the part that defines how products must be designed and assessed, applies from December 2027.
Europe is not the only one moving. Japan has set the rules for a new scheme that rates the security of companies in its supply chains, and the U.S. is set to require connected consumer devices bought by federal agencies to carry its Cyber Trust Mark label from January 2027. These are softer instruments, though: a voluntary rating, a label, a procurement rule. The CRA is binding law, with CE marking, fines, and a reporting clock, and it applies to anyone who sells into Europe, wherever they are based. As usual, the EU leads in regulation, for good and for bad.

This year's winner was Dr. Ning Xu, from Tsinghua University in China, whose video captured tiny cilia beating in the airways of a child with primary ciliary dyskinesia, a rare respiratory disorder.
But Xu's entry raised several concerns among members of the scientific community. Some researchers said there were abnormalities in the structure and size of the cells and that their features appeared and disappeared in a way not seen in cellular biology.
One associate professor at the University of Florida said some of the structures "pop in and out of existence" and the cilia "appear from nowhere," which are classic indications that a video was AI-generated.
A more damning discovery came from PhD student Ian Donovan at UT Southwestern Medical Center, who said the source image appeared to contain a distinctive watermark indicating it had been AI-generated. Two former competition judges also raised concerns about the clip's legitimacy.

articles.title: Remédio moderno para enxaqueca acende alerta sobre risco em gravidez
articles.summary:
Uma classe de medicamentos usados na prevenção da enxaqueca foi associada a um risco cerca de 40% maior de aborto espontâneo nas primeiras 20 semanas de gravidez. O estudo, publicado na revista JAMA Neurology, analisou dados de 7.579 gestações.
A pesquisa investigou anticorpos monoclonais que bloqueiam o CGRP, molécula envolvida nas crises de enxaqueca e em processos importantes da gravidez. Os resultados não comprovam que os medicamentos causem abortos espontâneos, mas levantam dúvidas sobre sua segurança durante a gestação.
Como agem os medicamentos
A enxaqueca nem sempre responde aos analgésicos comuns. Em 2018, uma classe de medicamentos injetáveis passou a oferecer uma alternativa para pacientes que não melhoram com tratamentos orais, como triptanos e ergotamina.
Esses medicamentos bloqueiam o CGRP, sigla para peptídeo relacionado ao gene da calcitonina. A molécula participa das crises de enxaqueca, mas também atua na regulação do fluxo sanguíneo, na implantação do embrião e no desenvolvimento da placenta. Essa participação em diferentes processos levou os pesquisadores a investigar uma possível relação entre o tratamento e complicações na gravidez.
O que revelou a pesquisa
Liderado pela epidemiologista Anick Bérard, do Centre Hospitalier Universitaire Sainte-Justine, no Canadá, o estudo utilizou registros de planos de saúde privados dos Estados Unidos, coletados entre 2018 e 2021.

articles.title: Google paid $90,000 for this bug, then waited two months to fix it
articles.summary:
Google paid $90,000 for this bug, then waited two months to fix it
Google took two months to patch an unauthenticated RCE vulnerability in its developer documentation infrastructure. The problem was a reused OAuth client secret: DevSite stored it in a Flask session cookie and used it to sign sessions. Anyone who recovered the secret could forge a valid cookie and execute Python code on the server.
Simon Köck, a software engineer at Otark GmbH, discovered the flaw in Google’s DevSite infrastructure, which is the shared platform behind developers.google.com plus several sibling documentation sites. Köck says the same signing secret worked across seven Google domains, although he publicly documents code execution only on developers.google.com.
Google rated the vulnerability S0, the top of its severity scale, and awarded Köck a $90,000 bounty.
Google rated the vulnerability S0, the top of its severity scale, and awarded Köck a $90,000 bounty. That figure reflects a $75,000 base payout for an S0 RCE in what Google classifies as a normal application tier, multiplied by 1.2 for exceptional report quality.
Köck confirmed unauthenticated RCE using a Python sleep payload, stopping short of running shell commands or accessing sensitive data, which leaves open the question of what an attacker could have done with the DevSite process’s privileges.

articles.summary:
Amid a flurry of product announcements and updates at this year’s Open Compute Project Global Summit, Intel is at the show to deliver an update on Crescent Island, the company’s forthcoming AI inference GPU. After outlining the chip’s architecture back at Hot Chips 2026, the company is offering a short update on the product today, outlining some of the chip’s final performance specifications along with giving the cards based on it a proper name. Going forward, Crescent Island will be sold as part of Intel’s GPU D-Series.
Speeds and Feeds: Crescent Island Nears Release
As a brief refresher, Crescent Intel’s is first commercial AI-focused data center GPU since Ponte Vecchio in 2021. With two of Ponte’s successors canceled over the last few years – Rialto Bridge in 2023 and then Falcon Shores in 2025 – Intel announced Crescent Island at least year’s OCP Global Summit as an interim product to target the AI inference market with a heavily cost and power-optimized part. The resulting chip is not meant to be on the same performance level as flagship chips such as NVIDIA’s Blackwell Ultra or AMD’s MI455X, but then it will be a lot smaller and cheaper as well.
Most recently, Intel delivered an update on Crescent Island back in August, where the company offered a fairly detailed look at the architecture behind the chip. articles.title: 30 años de despliegue de cables submarinos, en un vídeo 20 segundos: así se ha tejido Internet bajo el mar desde 1999
articles.summary:
Qué paradoja que para disfrutar de ese internet por todas partes y libre de cables hayamos llenado mares y océanos precisamente de cables para que la fibra vaya de continente a continente. De hecho, aproximadamente el 99 % del tráfico internacional de internet viaja bajo esas grandes masas de agua, según Naciones Unidas. Hay un "Google Maps" de los cables submarinos donde ver todos los hilos que hay y los que están por hacer y no son pocos, pero cómo ha cambiado ese mapamundi del cable en los últimos 30 años.
Porque el mapa de TeleGeography muestra 694 cables y subiendo, pero a principios de los dosmil la cifra era casi la décima parte. Por eso Mapped Earth, el interesantísimo proyecto de Aaron J. Becker del que ya os hemos hablado en varias ocasiones, como en este mapa interactivo de faros o este otro de la oscilación de los ríos en la península Ibérica, ha recogido la evolución de los cables submarinos de internet desde 1999 y lo ha sintetizado en un vídeo de apenas 20 segundos que acaba en 2029.
Los cables submarinos son la columna vertebral de internet, la nube y todo lo que conlleva (por ejemplo, la banca). Pese a estar en el fondo marino, expuestos y sin vigilancia, se producen unos 150-200 fallos al año (según el Comité Internacional para la Protección de Cables), una cifra estable para lo que está creciendo esta maraña. Retail giant Ahold Delhaize, one of the world's largest food retail chains, confirmed today that it was forced to take some systems offline after a "cybersecurity incident."
As a wholesale company and multinational retailer, Ahold Delhaize operates more than 9,400 local stores across Europe, the United States, and Indonesia, employs nearly 400,000 people, and serves around 60 million customers each week through physical retail locations and online.
Ahold Delhaize reported yearly net sales of over $104 billion in 2024, and it owns a wide range of brands, including Delhaize, Maxi, Mega Image, Albert, bol, Alfa Beta, Etos, Gall & Gall, and Profi in Europe, and Food Lion, Stop & Shop, Giant Food, and Hannaford in the American market.
In a succinct press release published earlier today, the company added that it's working to mitigate the incident and that its stores are open to customers.
"Ahold Delhaize is experiencing a security issue within its network. Our teams are taking steps to assess and mitigate the issue. This includes taking some systems offline to help protect them. At this time, our stores are open and serving customers," it said.
"Protecting our infrastructure in the best interest of our customers, associates and partners is a top priority. We apologize for any inconvenience this issue may have caused customers and partners."

articles.title: Ein Planet aus Sternenasche: So entstand die neue Welt um einen Weißen Zwerg
articles.summary:
Planet der zweiten Generation: Wie sich um einen toten Stern eine völlig neue Welt bildete
Wissenschaftler:innen der britischen Universität Warwick haben einen Planeten identifiziert, der den Weißen Zwerg HS 0209+0832 umkreist. Wie in einer im Wissenschaftsmagazin Nature Astronomy veröffentlichten Studie zu lesen ist, handelt es sich dabei um einen sogenannten Planeten der zweiten Generation. Die detaillierten Hintergründe zu dieser Beobachtung hat die Universität ergänzend in einer Mitteilung zusammengefasst. Bislang wurde die Existenz solcher Himmelskörper lediglich im Umfeld von Pulsaren vermutet, jedoch noch nie bei einem Weißen Zwerg nachgewiesen.
Ein Weißer Zwerg und seine ungewöhnliche Hülle
Weiße Zwerge sind die stark verdichteten Überreste von Sternen, die ihren nuklearen Brennstoff vollständig verbraucht haben. Sie verfügen über eine sehr hohe Gravitation, die normalerweise dafür sorgt, dass schwere chemische Elemente schnell in das Innere absinken.
Wenn Astronom:innen dennoch schwere Elemente in der Atmosphäre eines Weißen Zwergs messen, ist das ein Indikator dafür, dass der Stern aktuell Material aus seiner direkten Umgebung anzieht. Bei gewöhnlichen Planeten der ersten Generation besteht dieses Material primär aus gesteinsbildenden Elementen wie Silizium oder Eisen, was sich mit der chemischen Zusammensetzung unserer Erde vergleichen lässt.

articles.summary:
Reddit user pays $35 for a crypto mining rig left in a garage and gets 54GB of VRAM at 65 cents per GB — the first test for 2017-era GPUs: a 35B-parameter AI model running locally at over 30 tokens per second
A rusty rig and a refused test, but all nine cards worked.
A Reddit post by user markpronkin (“OP”), titled “54gb vram for 35$,” says the user purchased an old crypto mining rig, originally discovered in a garage, for a negotiated 3,000 rubles, or about $35. The rig was rusty, and the buyer “had zero idea if it works, so did the seller,” with a pre-purchase test request refused. However, on the first try, all nine Nvidia P106-100 GPUs, with 54GB of VRAM between them, worked. The initial test: a successful local run with the 35-billion-parameter model Qwen3.6-35B-A3B in Ollama, which operated at over 30 tokens per second.
The rig was discovered in a “damp garage” the seller had purchased years earlier, then listed on Avito, a Russian classifieds site. The OP had concerns about whether or not the rig would work and offered to test it and pay more if it functioned, but the seller refused, and the price was negotiated down without a test. The cost was low enough to take the risk, the buyer said. Even in the case the rig worked, performance was imbalanced, as the main system has a weak Celeron CPU with very little system memory.

articles.title: California sues major 3D-printing filament maker over claims it deliberately catered to ghost gun enthusiasts
articles.summary:
A hot potato: California's long-running battle against 3D-printed guns has just seen San Diego County, acting on behalf of the state, sue Polymaker LLC, one of the world's largest 3D-printing filament manufacturers. The lawsuit claims that Polymaker intentionally markets and sells its filament to Californians with the express purpose of creating illegal ghost guns.
The complaint, which was filed on October 5 in San Diego County Superior Court, acknowledges that 3D printing filament is not illegal. However, it alleges that Polymaker intentionally marketed its product toward ghost gun aficionados so they could turn its filament into a regulated "firearm precursor part."
California law describes a firearm precursor part as including an article marketed or sold to the public to become or be used as the frame or receiver of a functional firearm once completed, assembled or converted.
The complaint adds that Polymaker monetized the ghost gun community by supporting and hiring Sean Aranda, also known as The 3D Print General. After he was banned from YouTube in 2023 over firearm policy violations, Polymaker offered him a job as Head of Customer Experience. He is now a Senior Technical Account Manager at the company.
The suit alleges that hiring Aranda was part of Polymaker's effort to target 3D-printed gun enthusiasts.
The complaint also points to affiliate payments and firearm-themed products as evidence that the company actively cultivated this particular market for its filament.

Japoneses baixam pornô no Torrent e recebem cobrança de R$ 15 mil
Produtoras de conteúdo adulto do Japão enviam notificações para usuários de BitTorrent.
O download de conteúdo pornográfico no Japão pode sair mais caro do que você imagina: usuários começaram a receber ofícios e multas de 500 mil ienes, o que dá cerca de R$ 15 mil em conversão direta. Em comum, os casos mais recentes incluem o uso do BitTorrent para obtenção do material.
Um homem de 40 anos, morador de Tóquio, passou a deixar o Torrent ligado durante a noite para copiar os vídeos adultos. Em maio, ele recebeu uma notificação judicial depois que uma Corte autorizou a identificação dele para os detentores de direitos autorais.
De acordo com o jornal The Mainichi, dados como nome, endereço e número de telefone foram entregues. Vinte dias depois, uma nova carta, dessa vez do advogado de uma produtora de vídeos, trazia uma cobrança de R$ 15 mil. Caso não pagasse, a firma tomaria as providências para ações no âmbito civil e criminal.
O homem procurou um advogado e está em negociações para reduzir o valor da cobrança.
Este é apenas um de inúmeros relatos similares. A Corte Distrital de Tóquio registrou um aumento nos processos para identificação de informações: de 814 em 2023 para 5.320 em 2025. Quase 96% dos processos de 2024 envolviam provedores de internet.

articles.title: iRhythm Data Breach Impacts at Least 360,000 People
articles.summary:
Medical equipment provider iRhythm is notifying more than 360,000 people that hackers stole their personal information.
The data breach was identified on June 8 and involved third-party-hosted business applications that stored certain iRhythm information, the company says.
During its investigation into the incident, iRhythm determined that hackers accessed and exfiltrated patient data from the affected applications between June 3 and June 8.
The compromised information includes patients’ names, addresses, email addresses, dates of birth, and phone numbers, as well as iRhythm account and device data, such as account numbers, serial numbers, insurance numbers, and dates of service.
Based on data breach notices iRhythm filed last week with regulators in several states, at least 360,000 individuals (298,647 in Texas and 69,526 in South Carolina) were affected. The total number of impacted patients is likely significantly higher.
In a June filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), the company said the hackers contacted it on June 9, threatening to leak the stolen information online unless a ransom was paid.
Last week, iRhythm said it currently has no evidence that the stolen information “has been or will be used to commit identity theft,” which suggests that it gave in to the extortionists.

articles.title: Ben Affleck tiene una nueva película en la que ha utilizado IA para "muchas cosas", pero no te va a decir cuáles
articles.summary:
Estamos en un punto en el que hay un acalorado debate sobre el uso de la IA. Hay muchas herramientas disponibles, lo que amplía los ámbitos en los que puede impactar, y el mundo del cine no se está quedando al margen. Hay críticos como Guillermo del Toro o Hayao Miyazaki, dos de los genios de este arte, pero también quien abraza la tecnología para crear series enteras o para sustituir los VFX. Y una de las voces con más peso en el debate del uso de la IA en Hollywood es la de Ben Affleck.
En su última película la ha "usado para muchas cosas", pero tiene claro que hay una línea roja y que dentro de unos años nos reiremos al recordar la IA como si fuera Terminator. El contrapunto es que Affleck defiende la IA... porque tiene una empresa de IA.
En corto. Hace unos días, en un evento de Bloomberg, comentó que para su nueva película para Netflix ('Animals') ha usado la IA "para muchas cosas". El giro es que se negó a detallar cuáles y su argumento es que, si el cine busca fomentar la ilusión de realidad, no tiene sentido desvelar el truco.
En el mismo evento, Affleck aseguró que lo que hay que hacer es fomentar el uso de la IA como una herramienta más siempre que se haga de forma ética y catalogó su nueva cinta como "muy humana". No pienses que es animación o algo como 'Star Wars' repleto de VFX, ya que 'Animals' es la historia de un candidato a la alcaldía de Los Ángeles cuyo hijo es secuestrado y tanto él como su mujer se implican en conseguir el rescate.

articles.title: Quand l'IA disparaît, les résultats s'effondrent : ce que révèle une étude sur ChatGPT et la persévérance
articles.summary:
Comment réagit notre cerveau face à l’intelligence artificielle (IA) ? La question se pose alors que cette technologie promet de nous faciliter le quotidien en nous assistant dans nos recherches, nos écrits, et diverses interrogations. Dans une étude portant sur 1 222 participants, on apprend qu’utiliser une IA plus de 10 minutes pourrait justement nous faire perdre une faculté : celle de persévérer face à un problème.
Le papier est signé par cinq chercheurs, dont Grace Liu (université Carnegie Mellon), première autrice, et Brian Christian, chercheur à l’université d’Oxford, auteur de The Alignment Problem (2020), qui réfléchit aux effets de l’IA sur nos esprits depuis une vingtaine d’années.
L’étude a été présentée à San Francisco lors de la Conference on Language Modeling (COLM), qui s’est tenue du 6 au 9 octobre. Pour y être acceptée, elle a été relue par des spécialistes extérieurs à l’équipe, ce qu’on appelle la relecture par les pairs (peer review). GPUs on Kubernetes are bring-your-own-everything, starting with the bill
If you run a Kubernetes platform, you’ve probably got at least one Grafana dashboard for resource visibility on your workloads. It shows what a container asked for versus what it used, making it relatively easy to point at the deployment that requested four cores and is only using half of one. If you break it down by namespace you get a rough idea which team is consuming what, which is what teams have been doing for CPU and memory for years and it mostly works.
Then people started putting workloads on GPUs and a lot of what we assumed would carry over didn’t. Almost every piece of visibility you take for granted on CPU and memory, GPUs make you build yourself. Your own metrics, your own accuracy, your own rules for splitting the bill. Which is what stings the most, since the GPU is the most expensive line on the bill.
Bring your own metrics
With CPU and memory, the kernel already tracks usage per container for you, so getting a per-pod number is basically free. GPUs on the other hand, don’t give you that. The tool everybody starts with, NVIDIA’s DCGM exporter, reports at the physical device level by default. This is fine when one pod has a GPU to itself, but the second you start sharing a GPU across pods, with time-slicing or MPS, DCGM gives every pod sharing that GPU the same value. So if three pods are sharing one GPU, all three look like they’re using the whole thing, and when you add it up you get 30…

articles.title: Inside AvisLoader: A Windows Malware Loader Built to Resist Disruption
articles.summary:
Varonis Threat Labs recently discovered AvisLoader, a new Windows loader named after the Latin word for bird. We found it on an exposed staging server alongside a ClickFix lure, supporting tools, and its Command Center.
The attack starts with a familiar ClickFix lure. A page posing as a document-signing request asks visitors to copy and run an attacker-supplied command on their machine.
The more interesting part is how AvisLoader stays connected. It communicates via Tox, an encrypted peer-to-peer (P2P) messaging network that carries commands and additional payloads from the operator.
That setup makes traditional domain-based takedowns harder. The command-and-control (C2) channel does not depend on a fixed domain or server address, and operators can keep the same identity when moving to another server.
The seller references this in a cybercrime forum listing, claiming the controller can be moved by copying its Tox save file, with clients following without the need for a domain.
In this post, we look at how AvisLoader works, the MITRE ATT&CK techniques it uses, and the indicators security teams can use to detect it.
Delivery through ClickFix and Cloudflare
The specific ClickFix lure we found alongside AvisLoader was hosted on Cloudflare Workers and made to look like a DocuSign signing request.
A fake “Manual verification” dialog claims “Verification is handled by Cloudflare” and asks visitors to paste a “verification code” into a terminal. It presents running the command as a s…

articles.title: Canonical Websites Disrupted in Second DDoS Attack This Year
articles.summary:
Canonical’s websites were disrupted last week by a distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attack, months after a larger attack hit the Ubuntu maker’s infrastructure.
The company confirmed the attack on October 8 in a post on the Ubuntu Discourse forum. “Canonical’s websites are under a sustained distributed denial of service attack,” the company said, adding that some services might not be reachable at times.
The disruption was limited to Canonical’s primary web properties, OMG! Ubuntu reported. These included ubuntu.com, canonical.com, the Ubuntu blog and developer site, and Ubuntu’s security advisory pages and API.
Developer-facing services such as Launchpad and the Snap Store did not appear to be affected.
Canonical said on October 9 that its team was still bringing affected services back, though most were accessible again. OMG! Ubuntu put the total downtime at a little over four hours.
The company has not publicly shared information on the size or origin of the cyberattack. No one appears to have taken credit for the DDoS attack.
Canonical was hit by a more disruptive attack in late April. Launchpad and the Snap Store were among the services taken down, and some users could not install Ubuntu updates. The company described that incident as a “sustained, cross-border attack.”
A hacktivist group calling itself The Islamic Cyber Resistance in Iraq – 313 Team claimed responsibility for that attack. It’s unclear whether the two incidents are connected.

Satya Nadella a publié ce week-end un texte intitulé "Models as Insider Risks in the Super Intelligence Era". L'idée est simple : on ne peut pas déléguer à un fournisseur de modèles la responsabilité de ce que fait une IA à notre place.
Un modèle d'IA surveillé comme un salarié aux accès étendus
Tout part d'un constat. Avec un logiciel classique, on peut remonter d'un comportement jusqu'à la portion de code responsable. Avec les modèles d'IA actuels, c'est impossible. articles.title: Orange vend 5 euros la promesse de ne plus ramer dans la foule : comment ça marche ?
articles.summary:
Envoyer une vidéo depuis un concert ou retrouver ses amis à la sortie d’un stade, c’est souvent mission impossible quand des milliers de smartphones se connectent à la même antenne. Orange pense avoir une solution : le Fast Pass 5G+. Cette option payante, lancée en France à 5 €, permet d’accéder à une partie du réseau mise de côté pour ceux qui l’ont achetée pendant une durée limitée.
Qu’apporte cette option ?
Comme l’explique Orange sur son site, l’abonné accède à « une bande dédiée au sein d’une cellule lorsque 80 % de la cellule est occupée ». Avec le pass, l’abonné accède à une bande réservée à ceux qui ont payé, dès que la foule commence à saturer le réseau. Orange ne dit pas si elle est prélevée sur la capacité commune ou ajoutée à celle-ci.
La technique qui permet ce découpage s’appelle le network slicing. Elle repose sur la 5G qu’Orange appelle 5G+ (correspondant à la technologie 5G SA ou Standalone) et qui dispose de son propre cœur de réseau au lieu de s’appuyer sur celui de la 4G. Le réseau physique reste le même, mais il peut être divisé en tranches virtuelles, chacune avec ses propres priorités. Cela explique pourquoi le pass exige un smartphone compatible 5G+ et une zone couverte par ce réseau.
Jusqu’à deux fois plus rapide, mais sans garantie
Orange promet des débits « jusqu’à deux fois plus rapides » grâce à cette bande dédiée, sans préciser, à notre connaissance, par rapport à quoi ce doublement est mesuré. Surtout, l’opérateur ne garantit aucun débit minimal…

articles.title: Hay un español que tiene 1.500 millones de euros y pocos saben quién es. Jesús Núñez empezó vendiendo un colegio a los 19 años
articles.summary:
¿Se puede ser millonario y ser un absoluto desconocido de la prensa diaria? Que se lo digan al legendario Masayoshi Son. O mejor, a Zhu Yiming o Liang Wenfeng, fundador de DeepSeek, ambos perfiles casi anónimos para la prensa europea. Porque hay fortunas que se reconocen por la etiqueta en una camisa y otras que solo se reconocen por un campus. La de Jesús Núñez Velázquez es de las segundas. En 2024, irrumpió en la prensa como el número 23 de hombres más ricos de España, con 1.600 millones de euros. Forbes estimó su riqueza a la baja en 2025, en 1.500 millones de euros para él y su familia. Fuera del sector educativo madrileño, casi nadie sabría ponerle cara.
Del cole a la universidad. Es segoviano, natural de Pecharromán (una localidad de apenas 10 habitantes perteneciente al municipio de Valtiendas). Llegó a Madrid hace más de medio siglo para estudiar Magisterio y Ciencias de la Educación. Y con apenas 19 años creó su primer colegio de preescolar y primaria en el barrio de San Blas. Bueno, más que crearlo la inauguró.
En 1993 fundó la Universidad Alfonso X el Sabio (UAX), que se presenta como la primera universidad privada no confesional de España. articles.title: Kontrollverlust berechenbar: Wenn lokale Sprachmodelle plötzlich gefährlich werden
articles.summary:
Physiker finden mathematische Formel: Wann lokale KI-Modelle plötzlich gefährlich werden
Die Nutzung von Sprachmodellen direkt auf Endgeräten wie Smartphones oder Tablets nimmt branchenübergreifend zu. Da diese sogenannten Edge-KI-Modelle lokal und ohne Cloud-Anbindung arbeiten, fehlen ihnen herkömmliche nachgeschaltete Sicherheitsfilter, sogenannte Guardrails.
Das birgt Risiken für Anwender:innen, die auf Offline-Modelle angewiesen sind, etwa im medizinischen, juristischen oder militärischen Sektor. Zwei Physiker der US-amerikanischen George Washington University wollen solche Risiken nun mit einer mathematischen Formel besser abschätzen.
In einer im Wissenschaftsmagazin Patterns veröffentlichten Studie präsentieren Neil F. Johnson und Frank Yingjie Huo eine Gleichung, die berechnen soll, wann ein Sprachmodell von einer angemessenen Antwort zu einer potenziell schädlichen Ausgabe kippen kann.
Edge-KI und das Problem der fehlenden Cloud-Sicherheitsfilter
Ein Teil heutiger KI-Schutzmechanismen greift erst während der Nutzung: etwa durch cloudbasierte Filter, Monitoring oder nachträgliche Sicherheitsupdates. Bei reiner Offline-Nutzung stehen solche externen Guardrails nicht zur Verfügung, sodass eine fehlerhafte oder gefährliche Ausgabe ungefiltert auf dem Bildschirm der Nutzer:innen erscheinen kann.
Besonders problematisch ist dies bei Fachpersonal, das aus Datenschutzgründen etwa keine Patientendaten oder Mandanteninformationen in die Cloud senden darf. Ohne laufende externe …

articles.title: The Yandex outage probably didn’t blitz Russian bots
articles.summary:
Multiple Ukrainian drone strikes over the last week have taken Russian data centers offline and reportedly caused online bot traffic to plummet — but in reality it’s probably not the kind of bot activity most people associate with Russia.
The Yandex outage probably didn’t blitz Russian bots
At least, not the troll traffic that blights social media.
A chart citing Cloudflare data has been circulating around social media platforms, showing a sharp decline in bot traffic following attacks on Yandex servers — a technology company often described as “Russia’s Google.” While many people are inferring that the chart refers to bot farms that push disinformation, conspiracy theories, and other harmful content across online platforms, reputed troll farm exposer antibot4navalny says the data “has nothing to do with social media.”
In a thread on X, antibot4navalny says the chart is actually measuring requests from automated Yandex web crawlers. These bots have broad uses, so while they can be used maliciously to hack user accounts and target people with spam, they’re also very commonly used to index websites for search engines and provide customer service support. The chart is also specific to Yandex-based traffic, and not bot activity from Russia at large — which remains largely unchanged around the data center attacks, according to Cloudflare.

articles.title: Bricksforge WordPress Plugin Vulnerability Exploited in the Wild
articles.summary:
A critical vulnerability in the Bricksforge WordPress plugin is being exploited in the wild, according to WordPress security company Patchstack.
The vulnerability is tracked as CVE-2026-85097 and it has a CVSS score of 9.8. Unauthenticated attackers can exploit it to upload arbitrary files and execute malicious code.
This can allow threat actors to take full control of the targeted WordPress websites.
The security hole was patched with the release of version 3.1.8.10. Versions 3.1.8.9 and earlier are affected.
Patchstack started seeing in-the-wild exploitation attempts on October 7.
Bricksforge is a commercial add-on for the Bricks visual site builder that layers extra tools onto WordPress sites, such as custom forms, animations, an email designer, and admin-area pages. Patchstack reported that it’s used by roughly 6,000 websites.
“Two clusters stand out in our telemetry,” Patchstack explained. “In the first, 44 IPs sent 56 requests with identical payloads within seconds of each other. In the second, three IPs tested 25 variations of PHP extensions and encodings against the same temporary file.”
The company added, “Both patterns point to automated exploitation over rotating proxies or distributed infrastructure. They do not, on their own, attribute the activity to a single threat actor.”
It’s not uncommon for threat actors to target WordPress vulnerabilities shortly after patches are released, including plugin flaws and weaknesses affecting WordPress itself.

articles.title: NASA vai investigar buraco na Lua que pode levar a uma caverna
articles.summary:
A NASA selecionou uma missão para investigar uma abertura na superfície da Lua que pode dar acesso a uma estrutura subterrânea maior. O projeto, chamado Geophysical Instruments for Marius Lunar pit Investigation (GIMLI), pretende estudar o poço Marius Hills Pit (MHP) diretamente no solo lunar, para determinar se ele se conecta a uma caverna formada por antigas atividades vulcânicas.
Localizado em uma região com histórico de atividade vulcânica, o buraco tem dimensões estimadas de até 150 pés (cerca de 46 metros) de profundidade e 300 pés (cerca de 91 metros) de largura. Cientistas acreditam que a formação pode ser uma abertura causada pelo desabamento do teto de um tubo de lava subterrâneo, estrutura que também pode ajudar a explicar a história geológica da Lua.
Como será a investigação da NASA
Até agora, o Marius Hills Pit foi estudado apenas por observações feitas a partir da órbita lunar. A missão GIMLI pretende avançar nessa investigação com o uso de um veículo robótico equipado com instrumentos especializados para analisar as características do terreno e identificar possíveis estruturas abaixo da superfície.
Entre os equipamentos previstos estão um radar de penetração no solo, sondas sísmicas e um gravímetro, sensor que mede a intensidade do campo gravitacional. O rover também contará com câmeras para registrar imagens das partes expostas do poço.

articles.title: Hackers hit European supermarket refrigeration systems, spoiling food and forcing stores to dump stock
articles.summary:
In a nutshell: Cyber attackers are causing major headaches for grocery shoppers across Europe. On Sunday night, hackers targeted refrigeration systems at around 150 Intermarché stores, forcing employees to toss out food that is no longer safe to consume. And that's only the tip of the iceberg.
A spokesperson for the supermarket chain told Bloomberg that attackers infiltrated controls for the cooling systems and activated the defrost mode, which heated them to 50 degrees Celsius, or 122 degrees Fahrenheit. Roughly six hours passed before employees noticed. By that time, all of the food in the coolers had been ruined.
The attack wasn't limited to Intermarché stores. According to Agence France-Presse, fewer than 100 Cooperative U stores were also hit. BMF added that some Leclerc stores were also impacted. La Dépêche reports that electronic pricing label systems were also impacted.
Bloomberg said the systems targeted in the Intermarché attack were managed by Danfoss. Just a few months back, security researchers with Team 82 published a report highlighting multiple vulnerabilities in Danfoss refrigeration controllers that could lead to this exact sort of attack. It is no surprise, then, that an attack materialized in the real world.
The immediate fallout from the attack isn't fully clear, outside of the obvious inconvenience to shoppers, supermarket employees, and food suppliers. Early reports pin the financial loss at around 300,000 euros, but that figure could climb much higher …

Ledger wallets are physical devices designed to securely store the private keys that control cryptocurrency assets and authorize transactions.

Bosman called LekkeSlaap a great example of what South African entrepreneurs could build with persistence and ambition.

articles.title: GitLab 19.4 Adds Goal-Driven Agents and Tighter Cost Controls
articles.summary:
GitLab has released version 19.4 of its DevSecOps platform, adding a goal-driven mode to GitLab Duo CLI, three hosted open-weight models, a larger set of Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools, and more detailed controls for AI spending. The release moves GitLab's agents beyond individual prompts and predefined flows, while keeping their actions within the permissions and approval rules already used by a project.
The new /goal command in GitLab Duo CLI, now in public beta, accepts an open-ended objective and continues working until it completes the task or reaches an iteration limit. One model implements the changes while a separate model checks progress against the stated goal. A developer can stop the run, change the goal, or redirect the agent. The work runs locally and retains the project's existing context and controls.
"This release takes agentic automation from something individual developers use to something an organization can scale at speed and under the controls already in place."
Manav Khurana, GitLab
GitLab's use of the word "verified" has a specific meaning here. The second model judges whether the result meets the natural-language goal; this is not formal verification of the code. The command can report work that it could not resolve, and the iteration limit prevents it from continuing indefinitely. Clear acceptance criteria therefore remain important, even though the developer no longer has to supervise every intermediate step.

articles.title: PaidHR finds 46 of 100 Nigerian workers earn below $150 monthly

The findings show a wide gap between the lower and upper ends of the salary scale. Of every 100 workers in the dataset, 46 earn below ₦200,000 ($150) a month, while 10 earn at least ₦1 million ($751.93).
“The shape of the distribution suggests that Nigeria’s formal workforce is not one evenly distributed middle class; it is increasingly a two-tier labour market,” Seye Bandele, PaidHR’s co-founder and chief executive officer, told TechCabal in an interview. “A large group is clustered around relatively low wages, alongside a much smaller professional group earning substantially more.”
Nigeria’s labour force participation rate rose to 79.5% in Q2 2024, and formal employment accounts for about 7.0% to 7.3% of the total employed workforce. However, only a fraction of the workforce earns a regular wage from an employer, according to the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS). For these workers, earnings depend on their job, experience, industries, and how their employers value their skills.

articles.title: The ecologist revealing the invisible networks that revive rainforests
articles.summary:
The ecologist revealing the invisible networks that revive rainforests
Massive tree-planting programs lead to unhealthy monocrop plantations. Daisy Dent aims to help forests rebuild themselves.
In a research station in central Panama, you can walk through a century of forest time, watching scrubby plots of adolescent trees give way to cathedral-like canopies of mature growth. Forest ecologist Daisy Dent, a senior scientist at ETH Zurich, oversees this sequence of plots across the Barro Colorado Nature Monument, some of which date as far back as the 19th century. Not one of the trees she surveys was planted by human hands. She maps, measures, and tracks each trunk that emerges, revealing how waves of tree life rise from bare earth.
Tropical forests like these are our planet’s biggest terrestrial carbon sink, accounting for around 40% of carbon stored on land. As part of an international network of researchers, Dent is deciphering the networks of animal and plant interactions that enable some forests to recover after destruction. The goal is a low-cost, high-impact alternative to typical carbon-crediting schemes, which plant huge areas with a single species of tree. For over a decade, her research has built a body of evidence that such large “monocrop” programs could be expensive mistakes—and that more resilient forests can rebound naturally in just a few decades, re-creating ecosystems that suck up vast quantities of carbon dioxide.

articles.title: Open-source project moves one step closer to letting you run PlayStation 5 games natively on PC
articles.summary:
What we know so far: The open-source AnyPS5 project has taken a major step toward its goal of letting gamers run PlayStation 5 games natively on Windows and Linux PCs. Hosted on GitHub, the project now reports 100% GPU shader instruction coverage, with all 1,166 tracked AMD RDNA 1 and RDNA 2 instructions implemented, thanks to contributions from more than 100 (human) developers alongside AI-generated code.
AnyPS5 has successfully decoded the GPU instruction set used by the PS5's "Oberon" SoC, which pairs an 8-core AMD Zen 2 CPU with a custom RDNA 2 GPU. The developers note, however, that only instructions recognized by the decoder were counted, while decoded opcodes absent from AMD's public list were not.
It's also worth noting that the system libraries aren't fully translated yet, with the latest data showing 3,052 of 3,535 functions, or 86.34%, implemented. The developers clarified that the list only covers functions already declared in the project's core/libs/prx directory and doesn't account for every function exported by the PS5 firmware..
For those unfamiliar, AnyPS5 is a compatibility layer that lets PS5 binaries run natively on PC by converting executables built for the PlayStation 5 into formats Windows or Linux can read, much like Wine or Proton. It works by translating the PS5's proprietary API calls, such as those for graphics, audio, or user services, into native calls on Windows and Linux.

articles.title: Amazon has over 1 million robot workers. What’s next for human employees?
articles.summary:
No organization in the world operates more robots than Amazon. The company already has more than 1 million robots working in warehouses around the clock to make tens of millions of same-day and one-day package deliveries happen on a daily basis—and Amazon is poised to significantly grow that robotic fleet in the coming years as it establishes new factories to churn out increasingly more capable robot workers.
Despite deploying so many robots, Amazon is also the second-largest corporate employer in the world, with more than 1.5 million full-time and part-time human workers, according to its 2025 annual report. Amazon executives say that the growing robot fleet has eased the burden on its human workforce by taking on the toughest fulfillment center tasks that carry the greatest risks of physical fatigue and injury. But labor advocacy groups and independent researchers point to evidence suggesting that warehouse automation driven by AI is not all upside for the humans who work alongside robots.
“For the last 100 years, most of the automation that we’ve seen usually happens away from workers—you’re taking that high-risk task away from the worker, and you’re doing so in a way that is not physically proximate,” Brian Greenwood, professor of business at George Mason University, told Ars. “The rise of collaborative robots really changes that dynamic for two reasons: one is that it is physically proximate, and two, the robot has the ability to dictate the pace of work.”

articles.title: EU CRA Readiness: 5 Steps Manufacturers Need to Take Now - EE Times
articles.summary:
Consumer, industrial, networking, semiconductor, and software manufacturers face a broad product-cybersecurity regulation for the first time.
The European Union Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) makes product cybersecurity a condition of EU market access. Although its main requirements don’t apply until December 11, 2027, manufacturers need to start to plan and budget now in order to be ready for that date. This article outlines five steps companies can take immediately.
Coordinating a company-wide effort takes time; products that need additional security features may require months of engineering and testing, and the conformity work itself is significant. Figure 1 below shows the workflow for conformity.
How much work can this become? In an example created using a methodology that you can tailor to your portfolio, an in-scope portfolio of 1,000 products is estimated to require 24,000 to 48,000 hours of manual conformity work. Our paper on implementing a full, companywide EU CRA program explains how to estimate the workload for your own portfolio.
The challenge goes beyond understanding the regulation. Tasks required include connecting the people who understand cybersecurity requirements with those who understand the products—and giving both groups the information, time, and resources to act.

Mars may be a hellhole, but the moon is not far behind
We’re still imagining building cities on the moon. There are just a few obstacles in the way.
Welcome to the second space race. You can be forgiven for experiencing déjà vu. Last time, it was the Soviet Union and the United States vying to be the first to plant some flags. Now it’s a sprint to the lunar surface between America and China—alongside a host of varyingly friendly and rival nations—plus a cornucopia of private spaceflight companies. And this time it looks like they’re getting ready to set up camp. There will be, the contenders say, bases on the moon, permanently inhabited castles under the stars.

Initial astronaut missions to the lunar surface, which the US is currently planning to start in 2028, will be focused on exploration and technological experimentation. articles.title: Dev used AI agents and more than 500 billion tokens to rebuild Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2's source code — 83% of the 2009 shooter's functions now match the original byte for byte
articles.summary:
Dev used AI agents and more than 500 billion tokens to rebuild Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2's source code — 83% of the 2009 shooter's functions now match the original byte for byte
The agents originally tried to cheat the developer’s check.
Developer Maurice Heumann details in his blog how AI agents were able to decompile Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 (2009), which the post calls only “a popular first-person shooter,” in an effort to rebuild its source code in C++, taking three months and over 500 billion tokens. The agents originally attempted to cheat a byte-for-byte check added after the first month of code ran, but it was “semantically wrong,” and now 99% of the game’s functions are present, with 83% matching the original.
Heumann’s goal since the beginning has been to produce an “accurate, stable and feature-complete recreation,” and he wrote on X less than two weeks ago that the game was fully playable. By his estimate, the project consumed 600–700 billion tokens. In another X post, he said he doesn’t pay for his own tokens but put the cost at about €1,200 with subscriptions or $200,000–$250,000 with API tokens.
The difficulty turned out to be not in producing the code but verifying it was correct, forcing the developer to create a check and to make sure the agents couldn’t game it. The other challenge, as he put it, was that “corporate America was here to ruin our fun.” Two earlier blog posts on the project have since been removed, and the video in his Sept. 30 X po…

Une obligation de traçabilité, des alarmes et de la maintenance à distance

Es ist ein Klassiker im Online- und stationären Handel: Wer ein defektes Gerät beim Händler reklamiert, bekommt oftmals gesagt, dass er sich doch bitte direkt an den Hersteller wenden möge, weil man ihm dort schneller helfen könne und man das Gerät ja ohnehin einschicken würde. Doch der Reparaturservice des Herstellers, der sich um solche Probleme kümmern soll, ist in diesem Fall nicht die erste Anlaufstelle, wie ein neues Urteil zeigt.
Klar, für den Händler ist es praktisch, wenn sich die Kund:innen mit dem Service herumärgern müssen, doch für diese bedeutet es oftmals zusätzlichen Aufwand. Es ist aber vor allem rechtlich problematisch, wenn damit die Verantwortung für die gesetzliche Gewährleistung auf den Hersteller abgeschoben werden soll.
Mediamarkt wurde nun seitens des Landgerichts Ingolstadt dieses Vorgehen untersagt. Im Verfahren des Verbraucherzentrale Bundesverbands (vzbv) gegen die MMS E-Commerce GmbH – das ist die Onlinetochter besagter Elektronikmarktkette – entschieden die Richter, dass die Aufforderung gegenüber den Kund:innen, Gewährleistungsansprüche direkt beim Hersteller geltend zu machen, irreführend ist. Das Urteil vom 24. Juli 2026 (Az. 1 HK O 1352/25) wurde in der vergangenen Woche veröffentlicht und ist noch nicht rechtskräftig.

articles.title: Why millions of Africans covered by networks stay offline
articles.summary:
Africa’s push to connect one billion people by 2030 faces a bigger challenge than network coverage: getting the hundreds of millions already within reach of a signal to use the internet meaningfully.
In 2025, about 550 million Africans, or 36% of the continent’s population, used the internet, up from 16% in 2015. That remains far below the global internet usage rate of 74%, underscoring the gap Africa must close to meet its regional digital inclusion goals. But the challenge is not simply extending network coverage. Most Africans who remain offline already live within reach of a mobile broadband signal, pointing to barriers such as device affordability, digital skills, and the perceived value of going online.
About 906 million Africans live in areas covered by mobile broadband but do not use mobile internet, according to a joint report by the Partnership for Digital Access in Africa and GSMA Intelligence. Another 122 million live in areas without last-mile mobile or fixed connectivity.
That distinction matters because Africa’s connectivity gap is no longer simply a story about towers, fibre, and coverage. It is increasingly about whether people can afford a device, see a reason to go online, trust digital services, or use them in ways that improve their lives.
Ghana, Egypt, and Niger illustrate three versions of that problem.

Wie in einer im Wissenschaftsmagazin Nature veröffentlichten Studie zu lesen ist, entsteht dieses langgestreckte Gebilde durch einen bisher in planetaren Atmosphären nicht beobachteten Mechanismus. Dieser physikalische Prozess, die sogenannte homogene Keimbildung, vollzieht sich gänzlich ohne die Anwesenheit von Kondensationskernen wie Staub oder Schmutzpartikeln.

Die aktuellen Computersimulationen eines Forschungsteams um Jorge Hernández-Bernal und Franck Forget von der französischen Sorbonne Université in Paris widerlegen dies nun. Sie zeigen, dass diese etablierte Grundannahme für die lange Arsia-Mons-Wolke schlichtweg nicht gilt.

These auctions work by advertisers bidding for the right to display an ad to a Grindr user after they receive profiling information from Xandr, which acted as the intermediary.
At the time, Xandr was a joint controller with Grindr, meaning it was responsible for how the data was used and should have required and obtained explicit consent from the data subjects for this processing.
Grindr is a location-based dating app primarily serving the LGBTQ+ community.

articles.title: Long-lost horror gaming cult classic P.T. gets a much-needed PC port
articles.summary:
For over a decade now, the only “official” way to play Hideo Kojima’s cult classic, P.T.—the long-discontinued “playable trailer” for Kojima’s canceled “Silent Hills” project—has been via one of the increasingly rare PlayStation 4s that previously downloaded a copy during its monthslong availability window. Now, though, one coder is helping to preserve the game with a porting tool that builds a playable x86 PC executable from the original PS4 files.
Coder Lorean Xavier said he was inspired to work on the “P.T. for PC” project “because P.T. deserved to keep existing somewhere other than on consoles that still have it installed.” The open source porting effort rebuilds the P.T. engine in C++ and Vulkan, using the original files from the PS4 game to re-create “every level, model, texture, sound, script and cutscene,” according to its GitHub listing. That means players without their own legitimate decrypted copy of the original P.T. will have to track one down in order to generate a playable PC version.
The reliance on real P.T. files makes this port more authentic than previous hobbyist efforts to re-create the look and feel of P.T. for a PC audience. And while PS4 emulators recently reached a point where they could run P.T. completely, this native port also sports extra features, like upscaling and frame-generation, a camera mode, experimental third-person and VR support, and a “museum” section where you can look at and listen to in-game assets (including “unused content”).
